newsitem.title: USA: U.S West spot power up on storm, higher gas prices.
newsitem.headline: U.S West spot power up on storm, higher gas prices.

text.p: Spot power prices in the western U.S. continued to move higher amid increased demand and a lack of on-peak sales by Bonneville Power Administration (BPA), market sources said Thursday.
Storm conditions throughout much of the Pacific Northwest and northern California added a psychological boost as well as some weather-related demand, sources said.
Colder than normal temperatures in southern California, the onset of the Christmas lighting season and trial runs of new transmission pricing requirements were also cited as bullish market factors.
Utilities began this week to test the inclusion of transmission prices in their own wholesale prices as required by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.

And, although only those utilities with long-term fixed price contracts are said to be burning natural gas for power generation, higher spot natgas prices were also seen pushing western electricity prices upward.
Firm, peak COB electricity for Friday was assessed at $34.00-35.00 per megawatt hour (MWH), up from $33.00-34.00 on Wednesday.
Firm, off-peak COB power for Friday was little changed at $19.00-20.00.
Next-day firm, peak power at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) was quoted $29.00-30.00, steady from Wednesday.
Friday firm, off-peak power at Mid-C was up slightly at $18.50-19.50.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity for Friday was quoted $29.00-30.00 per MWh, up from $27.00-28.00. Firm, off-peak PV power was at $17.00-18.00.
Next-day firm, peak prices at Four Corners were quoted $29.00-30.00 per MWh, while firm off-peak was assessed at $18.00-19.00.
